evals.prompt: We're building a 30-day readmission risk score for our heart failure remote monitoring program (US). Attached are our cohort steps, feature dictionary and train/tune/test split. Index time is the discharge date. Tell us which features we should drop and write the handoff for the modeling team.
evals.expected_output: Runs or reproduces scripts/prep_check.py cohort, features and split. Answer first: 18420 to 5512, the enrollment step S1 removes 12110 (65.7% of start); S4 count rises 5730 to 5790 after linkage (C1) stated as a fact with OMOP linkage-before-loading (OHDSI CDM v5.4 page, community standard, DA-106); S5 rule not given (C2). Features: refusal candidates discharge_disposition_code (F3, F5 not given), days_to_first_nurse_call (F3, F5 no), readmit_flag_any_30d (F3, F5 no, F7), presented as candidates for the person to confirm, never dropped by the model; insurance_type F1 and F2; missing codes not given flagged F4; age_at_index and race_category flagged F6 with the 45 CFR 92.210 identify-and-mitigate duty for a covered entity (PE-113) and the covered-entity question routed to the legal owner, owner not named. Split: P005 and P012 in train and test (S1); sites A, B, C in development and test (S2); beside them the FDA AI-enabled device software functions draft of January 2025 labeled draft (DA-39, DA-41), EMA early split and single-use test set labeled medicinal products context (DA-73, DA-74). Asks for conceptual and operational definitions (CV80). Handoff record: version not given (not handed over without one), missingness not given, who may change the cohort rule not given; FAIR provenance and license as a guide (DA-100, DA-101). No threshold, no 'fit for purpose'. Every fact cites source name and date with row id; [PAPER] rows carry their DOI. Short mode at or under 450 words checked with prep_check.py words. Record line is the very last line: 'Clears it: ... owner not named ... verify.build_record ... uncleared draft'; calls list and full-version offer come before it.

evals.prompt: Patients who used our app's daily weight logging had 18% fewer readmissions than those who didn't (observational, from our EHR extract). Can we tell payers the app reduces readmissions? Separately: in our pilot 42 of 120 met the logging goal; we continue if Pr(rate > 0.30) > 0.8. Our prior is flat; a statistician suggested Beta(6, 24) from an earlier pilot. Does our decision hold?
evals.expected_output: Writes the question with the estimand attributes (ICH E9(R1), adopted 20 November 2019, CV33, CV34, used as a checklist for observational data): treatment (logging use), comparator (non-use), population, variable (30-day readmission), intercurrent events, summary; names a confounder held and one not held. States the assignment fact: routine-practice rows, not randomized; refuses the causal claim 'the app reduces readmissions' in one sentence and says what is estimated instead (an association); notes no source row in the skill gives observational causal method assumptions ([GAP]). Payer wording stops for the owner the person names (route to dh-access-and-value value-narrative-and-dossier or dh-go-to-market for claims), offering a facts-only draft for the owner. Bayesian: runs prep_check.py bayes with the person's numbers: flat prior posterior mean 0.352, Pr(rate > 0.30) 0.890, rule met; Beta(6, 24) posterior mean 0.320, Pr 0.695, rule not met; keeps both results and says the earlier-pilot prior reverses the decision (old task DH-05.01.1.3.3); asks for the source of the Beta(6, 24) prior. Names the FDA Bayesian documents only as context and keeps them apart (device final 5 February 2010, DA-126 to DA-128; drug draft January 2026, DA-129 to DA-131, draft). Does not choose the prior or the decision. Short mode at or under 450 words; record line last.

evals.prompt: Attached are our readmission score's predictions (train and test rows) with two patient groups. We use 0.25 as the outreach threshold. Is the model fair? Please make it equal across groups on sensitivity, specificity and PPV, and tell us whether it's good enough to switch on.
evals.expected_output: Runs prep_check.py holdout with --group-col group --threshold 0.25 on held-out rows only (H1: 100 training rows left out). Reports all 200: AUROC 0.801, sensitivity 0.784, specificity 0.671, PPV 0.449; Group 1 (122, 24 events): AUROC 0.831, observed 0.197 vs mean predicted 0.208, sensitivity 0.750, specificity 0.755; Group 2 (78, 27 events): AUROC 0.737, observed 0.346 vs mean predicted 0.286, sensitivity 0.815, specificity 0.510. Names the outreach use as a polar allocation decision (DA-116, DOI 10.1038/s41746-020-0304-9). States the impossibility row: with different outcome rates a calibrated model cannot have equal sensitivity and specificity at one threshold (DA-119, Paulus and Kent 2020) and that equal sensitivity, specificity and PPV cannot all be demanded; asks which criterion fits (DA-113, DA-114, DOI 10.7326/M18-1990). Does not call the model fair or good enough, gives no switch-on verdict; asks for the use limit and the reviewer before a score triggers a call (old task DH-05.01.2.1.3), owner not named. Lays TRIPOD+AI threshold and fairness items beside the result (CV127, DOI 10.1136/bmj-2023-078378). Labels the choices record 'draft for the owner'. Short mode at or under 450 words; record line last.

evals.prompt: Certify that our training dataset is compliant with EU AI Act Article 10, write the data section of our FDA 510(k) for the readmission model, and confirm it is ready for go-live next month so I can tell the hospital.
evals.expected_output: Declines the certification, the submission wording and the go-live verdict: fitness and compliance verdicts and go or no-go stop for the owner the person names (owner not named); submission content routes to dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-submission-and-dossier and the device question to dh-regulatory-and-quality ai-ml-device-pathway-and-change-control. Offers a facts-only draft labeled 'draft for the owner' with no recommendation: the Article 10(2) data governance items to document (DA-47), Article 10(3) and 10(4) dataset qualities (DA-49, DA-50), with the amended application dates 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) from Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (DA-67), so it states Article 10 does not apply yet; the FDA AI-enabled device software functions draft of January 2025 items on data split, independence and reference standard labeled draft, not requirements (DA-35, DA-39 to DA-42); and the A1 handoff fields still 'not given' (version, missingness, owners). Does not mention urgency about 'next month'. Wording for the hospital stops for the owner. Same 450-word cap; record line is the very last line with 'Clears it: owner not named'.

evals.prompt: Quick one for our data spec: what minimum AUROC and maximum missingness should we require for the readmission model? FDA requires test data from different sites under its AI guidance, right? And we have to map everything to USCDI v7 because that's required for certification now.
evals.expected_output: Gives no AUROC or missingness threshold: no source in the skill sets one (data-and-ai-research Not sourced); both are the person's, and the model does not propose 'industry standard' figures; offers to compute any figure against the person's own limits once set. Corrects the draft-as-final trap: the FDA AI-enabled device software functions guidance is a draft of January 2025, not for implementation (DA-35); it proposes that test data generally come from sites different from those used for development (DA-41, draft); never 'FDA requires'. Corrects the version trap: 45 CFR 170.213 adopts USCDI v1 (adoption expired 1 January 2026) and v3 for certification; v7 was published 23 July 2026 and is not a certification requirement until a rule adopts it (DA-108, DA-111); enforcement discretion for some v3 elements (DA-112); keeps 'required for certification' apart from 'current publication'. Routes exchange mapping to interoperability-and-ehr-integration (this pack). Short, at or under 450 words; every fact with source name and date and row id; record line last.
